v1.feedback: The rubber-band concept lands — radial stretch scaled by generation with the amber flash is a legible swerve that genuinely mutates the L-system parent rather than just recoloring it. Two things hold it back: the snap cycle is a fixed sine wave (stretch → overshoot → settle → repeat), so after 10 seconds the surprise is gone — consider making the snap event-driven or aperiodic with varying intensity so it stays surprising. The palette shift to amber during snap is good but the rest-state green-to-lime gradient reads a bit flat; try pushing the bark color darker and the tip lime slightly cooler to widen the tonal range without adding hue chaos.

v2.feedback: The L-system tree reads clearly as a tree within 2 seconds and the rubber-band snap mechanic is a genuine formal swerve — aperiodic radial stretch with squash-and-overshoot is well-engineered and earns its compute. The bark→sage→mint palette is restrained and pleasant, though the amber snap flash could be more visible; consider briefly boosting point size during peak snap so the color shift registers before it fades. The camera start at (8,4,22) leaves the tree a bit small in frame — pull in to ~(6,3,16) or bump FOV so the canopy fills more vertical space at rest.
